content.text: {"primary_meaning":"Consecration or divine appointment—being set apart, authorized, and empowered by God for a sacred office or service. In Christian interpretation, the anointing oil commonly symbolizes the presence and empowering work of the Holy Spirit, especially in relation to Christ and, derivatively, believers.","primary_basis":["Exodus 28:41; 29:7; 30:22-30; Leviticus 8:10-12 — priests and sacred objects are anointed and consecrated to God.","1 Samuel 10:1,6; 16:13 — kings are anointed for office, with Saul and David receiving the empowering activity of God's Spirit.","1 Kings 19:15-16 — kings and Elisha the prophet are appointed through anointing.","Psalm 2:2; 45:7 — the Lord's anointed is associated with divinely appointed kingship.","Isaiah 61:1; Luke 4:18-21 — anointing by the Spirit signifies appointment and empowerment for the Messiah's mission.","Acts 10:38 — God anoints Jesus with the Holy Spirit and power.","2 Corinthians 1:21-22 — God establishes and anoints believers, closely associated with the gift and seal of the Spirit.","1 John 2:20,27 — believers' anointing is commonly interpreted as the Holy Spirit's abiding presence and instruction."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Messianic kingship: “the Anointed One” is a royal title identifying Jesus as the
